title: Optimal Two-Round Input Difference for Full-S-Box LowMC
summary: For random-layer full-S-box LowMC, the expected inactive-S-box count is experimentally verified, but the exact two-round optimal input difference remains unresolved.

formal_statement.body: For full-S-box LowMC with a randomly generated linear layer, determine an input difference that activates exactly one S-box in the first round and maximizes the total number of inactive S-boxes across the first two rounds, equivalently minimizing the number of active S-boxes there. An exact optimum is difficult to obtain for a random linear layer; the available analysis instead computes the expected number of inactive S-boxes in the general case and verifies that expectation experimentally.

scope.domain: Differential cryptanalysis of two-round S-box activity in full-S-box LowMC.
assumptions: The LowMC linear layer is randomly generated.
The chosen input difference activates exactly one S-box in the first round.
parameters: Inactive S-box count across the first two rounds: the objective to maximize
scope.unresolved_remainder: Determine an exact optimal input difference rather than only the experimentally verified expected inactive-S-box count for the general case.

citations.label: Cryptanalysis of Full LowMC and LowMC-M with Algebraic Techniques

progress.summary: The source states that a randomly generated linear layer makes an accurate optimum difficult to obtain. It instead calculates and experimentally verifies the expected inactive-S-box count in the general case, without resolving the exact optimum.
citation_labels: Fukang Liu et al., Cryptanalysis of Full LowMC and LowMC-M with Algebraic Techniques
